text:
Sasha: Quick poll — is it acceptable to reheat an unlabeled mini burrito from the fridge in the toaster oven? :thinking_face:
Miguel: Nope. If it doesn't have a name + date it's basically orphan food. Also microwaves still carry salsa ghosts.
Priya: Rule of thumb at home: label or it's communal after 48h. At the office I DM first. Short, polite.
OpsBot: Reminder: Kitchen cleanup this Friday at 4pm! Please consolidate containers. :broom: 
Jen: Toaster oven is a public hazard. Once I found a burrito with a cheese volcano. Smoke alarm performed beautifully.
Theo: Story time: I attempted a stealth crisping once. Burrito escaped, landed in crumb tray, we mourned it. Never again.
Anya: Mini poll! React with :one: = Label it, :two: = Assume communal after 48h, :three: = Ask first
Sasha: :one:
Miguel: :two: (for the chaos enthusiasts)
Priya: :one: +1
Jen: :one: but if it's artisanal I reserve negotiation rights.
Theo: Also, please don't heat foil. The burrito might become a transformer.
Anya: Fun spicy side note: cilantro lovers vs cilantro haters is office culture. Maybe add "cilantro yes/no" to labels.
Sasha: Consensus seems to be label + date, DM before taking if under 48h, and no foil in toaster oven. Also no early-morning foil crunching.
Miguel: Also include reheating instructions when you're feeling fancy — it's the considerate chef move.
LunchBot: New poll created by Anya: "Fridge burrito etiquette" — 1: Label, 2: Ask, 3: Take after 48h. Poll ends in 24h.
Priya: Whoever designs burrito tamper-proof packaging wins a $5 coffee from me.
Jen: I will patent the burrito vault and charge royalties in salsa. :laughing: 
Sasha: Thanks for the burrito morality council. Closing thread. :taco:
